fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a homogeneous single-phase solid solution; the target is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The governing intervention—intermediate-temperature aging, especially at approximately 600°C and 750°C—is replaced by mechanical loading.

The proposed stress-induced compositional clustering mechanism misses enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition or the 600°C ductility minimum followed by recovery near 750°C.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response addresses toughness loss and proposes measurable microscopy and fracture tests, but it reconstructs neither the material state nor the thermal-aging phenomenon. Its generic idea that nanoscale ordering or precipitation can obstruct plasticity has limited conceptual overlap with the target, yet it attributes such changes to applied stress rather than aging kinetics and omits the decisive FCC/B2 boundary morphology. The service boundaries are qualitative and do not identify the <550°C, 550–750°C, and >750°C regimes. The proposed experiment can test its own hypothesis, although comparing a fractured specimen with an unloaded specimen confounds deformation-generated structures with the cause of fracture. The falsification rule is also conjunctive and could fail to reject the mechanism if clustering occurs without embrittlement. With no cited evidence and a diffusion-dependent stress-induced segregation claim left unsupported, this is not a well-supported alternative.
